newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK to build Western Corridor passenger rail first.
newsitem.headline: HK to build Western Corridor passenger rail first.

text.p: The Hong Kong government said on Wednesday it would move forward with the domestic passenger line of its proposed Western Corridor Railway first, leaving the cross-border and freight lines to a later date.
Secretary for Transport Gordon Siu said he anticipated construction of the passenger line linking the northwestern New Territories with downtown Kowloon could begin in mid-1998.

"On the basis that land resumption, clearance and phased handing over of sites would proceed in parallel with construction, the project might be completed by end-2002 to Yuen Long and by September 2003 to Tuen Mun," he said.

"The project cost as estimated by our consultants would be in the region of HK$50 billion and the KCRC (government-owned Kowloon-Canton Railway Corp) would require direct government support of some HK$24 billion," he said.
These figures will need to be further refined as KCRC proceed with their technical studies, he said.

Siu added construction of the domestic passenger line first reduced land resumption and clearance requirements by some 40 percent compared with building all three lines, reducing land resumption costs from about HK$5.4 billion to HK$3.5 billion.

He said the passenger line would go ahead due the urgent need for it, while the freight and cross-border lines would be left until later as the government was still some way from reaching definitive conclusions on their development and timing.
Siu also said the Mass Transit Railway Corp's (MTRC) Tseung Kwan O Extension should be constructed, and that its Quarry Bay Congestion Relief Works would be implemented urgently.

He said government-owned MTRC estimated the cost of the extension, based on an opening date of mid-2002, to be HK$25 billion, while the relief works, based on a completion date of December 2000, would cost HK$4.2 billion.
The MTRC proposed to finance the two projects by itself without financial support from Government, he added.
Siu said the government would finalize with both KCRC and MTRC the detailed project scope, financing and implementation programme for the passenger rail and extension projects.
"We will proceed with all necessary preparations leading to the drawing up of project agreements with the two corporations for approval in 1998," he said.
